topics.label: Lecture Introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes the students and outlines the lecture's focus on the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Principles of Innate Immune Recognition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the core concepts of how the innate immune system detects infection and cellular damage through PAMPs, DAMPs, and germline-encoded pattern recognition receptors.

topics.label: Pattern Recognition Receptor Families and Signaling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail specific PRR classes, such as Toll-like receptors, Nod-like receptors, and inflammasome complexes, alongside their downstream intracellular signaling mechanisms.

topics.label: Cellular Activation, Leukocyte Recruitment, and Systemic Inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how sentinel cells trigger local and systemic immune responses, direct leukocyte extravasation into tissues, drain antigen to lymph nodes, and can cause systemic pathologies like sepsis when overactivated.

topics.label: Resolution of Inflammation, Tissue Repair, and Chronic Inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the active and passive mechanisms that terminate acute inflammation, the processes of tissue repair, and the development of chronic inflammatory states including granuloma formation.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the lecturer's concluding remarks and previews the subject of the upcoming lecture.
